title: Introduce compatibility proxy that rewrites Accept-Schema and stabilizes streaming event enums for legacy clients
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation:
Older customers and OpenAI-compat SDKs frequently send requests without the new Accept-Schema header and rely on legacy streaming event types (e.g., delta/text fragments vs. structured 'output' envelope). After rolling out structured-output v3 we observed a class of integration breakages where legacy clients either face silent parse errors or spike error rates when the server emits new enum tokens in streaming frames.

Summary of changes:
- Add an in-process compatibility proxy layer in the redwood-openai-compat service that rewrites legacy requests into the canonical v3 schema at the edge when Accept-Schema is missing or set to an older version. The proxy is opt-in via feature flag but enabled for the canary cohort.
- Translate streaming frames from v3 structured-event envelopes back into legacy streaming event shapes for clients that indicate legacy schema via Accept-Schema or a missing header. This includes mapping new enum values (e.g., structured_output/FINISHED -> "done", structured_output/DELTA -> "delta_text") and adding a small delta buffer to reorder frames that had changed semantics.
- Introduce a short-lived shim for tool/function-calling: older callers expect a flat `tool_call` field; the proxy will normalize v3 function_call objects into that shape.
- Add end-to-end integration tests that run both legacy and updated SDK fixtures against the proxy to validate no behavioral regressions.
- Observability: new metrics for `compat.proxy.rewrites_total`, `compat.proxy.stream_mapped_total`, and a trace span `compat.proxy.rewrite` to help identify rewrites in production.

Design notes / tradeoffs:
- We intentionally keep rewriting logic lightweight (string/enum maps and shallow object reshapes) rather than deep model-guided transformations to reduce latency impact and avoid semantic drift.
- Streaming mapping introduces a 1-2ms per-frame overhead on average (measured in canary) due to buffer/resequence logic; this is acceptable for canary and can be disabled per-tenant.
- The feature flag gate allows us to flip the proxy per-region or per-account during rollout.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged canary in prod (5% traffic) for 48h with strict alerting on any increase in 4xx/5xx for streaming endpoints.
- Expand to 25% for a week if no regressions; full enable after 2 weeks.
- Deprecation schedule for older SDKs will be communicated: we will advertise a soft deprecation of missing Accept-Schema header in 90 days giving customers time to upgrade.

Testing done:
- Unit tests for enum mapping and object reshaping (coverage ~95% on compat module).
- Integration tests using recorded legacy SDK sessions that previously failed against structured-output v3; all pass.
- Load-tested proxy under synthetic streaming workloads: median added latency 1.8ms/frame; p95 6ms/frame.

Files changed (high-level):
- cmd/compat-proxy/main.go: new proxy bootstrap and feature-flag config
- internal/compat/proxy.go: core rewrite logic and streaming mapper
- internal/compat/mappings.go: enum and object mapping tables + tests
- api/compatibility/accept_schema_middleware.go: header negotiation middleware
- integration/legacy-fixtures/*: new legacy client fixtures and golden recordings
- observability/metrics.yaml: new metric defs and dashboard snippets
- docs/compat/README.md: rollout instructions and behavior specs

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests with legacy fixtures
- [x] Metrics and traces added
- [x] Feature-flagged with default off for tenants
- [x] Docs and rollout plan

Related work:
- Follow-on work scheduled to add a telemetry ping from upgraded SDKs to help us target tenants during the 90-day deprecation window (ENG-8239).

Notes:
- This PR is designed to be a short-term compatibility layer; teams should still migrate to explicit Accept-Schema negotiation to avoid relying on server-side heuristics.

release_notes: Adds a temporary compatibility proxy that rewrites legacy requests and streaming frames to preserve behavior for older SDKs when Accept-Schema is missing. Feature-flagged and can be disabled per-tenant. New metrics added for monitoring.
